A.note: Hazy, pale sky and milky water give flat, low-contrast lighting. The rock is the most natural-looking of the three, but the scene feels like a miniature model. The airport apron is a large, empty grey field.

B.note: Clouds and a blue gradient sky add depth, and the water is richer. The warmer buildings help. The rock is slightly more saturated, and the water edge looks a bit plasticky. The distant headland is still hazy, which keeps some atmospheric depth. The foreground remains a flat grey slab.

C.note: This has the strongest colour and contrast, with a deep blue sea and clear clouds. The distant landmass is dark green and heavy, with a hard edge and a sharp reflection. That reads as pasted-on and breaks the depth falloff. The foreground is the same flat grey as the others.

why: B has the best balance: lively sky and water plus believable atmospheric haze on the distant land, where C's distant island is too dark and hard-edged and A is washed out.
top_fix_for_best: Break up the empty grey airport apron and foreground with texture (tarmac wear, markings, parked aircraft, vehicles and ground-level clutter). Also add shadow and contact detail under the buildings so they stop reading as miniature blocks.
